headline_marked: [[XCorp sends C&D letters]] to Nitter and XCancel, shutting down open-source projects
headline: XCorp sends C&D letters to Nitter and XCancel, shutting down open-source projects
summary: XCorp has issued cease and desist letters to Nitter and XCancel, citing alleged data scraping and rules violations. This move effectively ends services that allowed users to view X posts without an account or tracking.
details: XCorp reportedly issued cease and desist letters to Nitter and XCancel on August 24th, citing alleged data scraping and violations of X's rules. Both open-source services have now ceased operations, with Nitter's maintainer seeking legal advice.

Nitter provided a way for users to read X posts without requiring an account, JavaScript, or ads, offering a privacy-focused and faster experience. XCancel was one of several platforms that relied on Nitter's service.

This isn't the first time Nitter has faced challenges from X (formerly Twitter); it previously went offline in January 2024 after guest account features were removed, only to find a workaround and return. However, this latest action is a direct legal challenge.

The move by XCorp has drawn criticism, particularly given Elon Musk's public stance as a "free speech absolutist," and X's own use of public data to train its AI, Grok. Consequently, accessing X content without an account has become significantly more difficult.

headline_marked: [[Ads have landed in Apple Maps]], and they are as bad as expected
headline: Ads have landed in Apple Maps, and they are as bad as expected
summary: Apple Maps is now showing ads for 'Suggested Places', a move that has been widely criticized by users. This comes despite an overwhelming majority of readers previously opposing ads in the service.
details: Apple Maps has started displaying advertisements within its "Suggested Places" section. These ads appear directly beneath business listings, marked with a small "Ad" label, promoting various services like sandwich shops, parking garages, and photography labs.

The introduction of ads has been met with significant user disapproval. A recent poll indicated that an overwhelming majority of 9to5Mac readers were against Apple integrating advertisements into its mapping service.

This move expands Apple's advertising efforts, which have been growing across its ecosystem. While ads are common in free services, their presence in a core Apple app like Maps is a point of contention for many users.
